title: CILIARY DYSKINESIA, PRIMARY, 2
alt_titles: CILIARY DYSKINESIA, PRIMARY, 2, WITH OR WITHOUT SITUS INVERSUS

intro.text: A number sign (#) is used with this entry because of evidence that primary ciliary dyskinesia-2 (CILD2) is caused by homozygous mutation in the DNAAF3 gene (614566) on chromosome 19q13.42.

paragraphs.text: Primary ciliary dyskinesia (PCD) is an autosomal recessive disorder characterized by chronic sinusitis, bronchiectasis, and subfertility. It is caused by defective ciliary function with ultrastructural abnormalities that include absent dynein arms, absent radial spokes, and disturbed ciliary orientation. Situs inversus occurs in 50% of cases (Kartagener syndrome), and the estimated incidence is 1 in 20,000 live births (Meeks et al., 2000).

checks.evidence_quote: Primary ciliary dyskinesia is an autosomal recessive condition

paragraphs.text: Mitchison et al. (2012) studied 10 patients with PCD from 3 consanguineous families: 2 families of Arabic origin and a UK-Pakistani family in which the parents were first cousins. The patients presented with neonatal respiratory distress, recurrent cough and wheezing, nasal discharge, chest infections, sinusitis, otitis media, nasal polyps, and bronchiectasis. Four of the 10 patients had situs inversus. Electron microscopy showed reduced or absent inner and outer dynein arms, and nasal cilia were immotile in all affected individuals. The authors noted that the disorder was associated with male infertility.

paragraphs.text: Meeks et al. (2000) carried out a genome scan in 5 Arabic families with primary ciliary dyskinesia. Using GENEHUNTER, they obtained a maximal multipoint lod score (HLOD) of 4.4 on chromosome 19q13.3-qter at alpha (the proportion of linked families) = 0.7. Recombinations at D19S572 and D19S218 defined a critical region of 15 cM.

paragraphs.text: In affected members of a consanguineous Arabic-origin family (UCL89) with CILD2, Mitchison et al. (2012) identified a homozygous mutation in exon 3 of the DNAAF3 gene, a c.323T-C transition resulting in a leu108-to-pro (L108P) substitution at a highly conserved residue. The variant was absent from 148 population-matched Arabic control chromosomes and from the dbSNP, 1000 Genomes, and NHLBI-ESP databases, and was predicted to be probably damaging. It segregated with recessive inheritance: the parents and unaffected sibs were heterozygous.

paragraphs.text: Mitchison et al. (2012) screened 112 additional PCD families. Affected members of a UK-Pakistani family (UCL71) in which the parents were first cousins showed linkage to the chromosome 19 locus and carried a homozygous 1-bp insertion in exon 6 of DNAAF3 (c.762_763insT). The insertion was predicted to cause a frameshift and premature termination (Val255CysfsTer12). It was absent from 172 UK-Pakistani control chromosomes and segregated with the disorder.

paragraphs.text: Using immunofluorescence, Mitchison et al. (2012) found that the outer dynein arm components DNAH5, DNAH9, and DNAI2 and the inner dynein arm light chain DNALI1 were absent from the respiratory cilia of patients with DNAAF3 mutations. In some patients, residual DNAH5 and DNALI1 were present in the apical cytoplasm. These findings suggested that DNAAF3 is required for the cytoplasmic preassembly of outer and inner dynein arms along the entire axoneme.

checks.claim: Using immunofluorescence, Mitchison et al. (2012) found that the outer dynein arm components DNAH5, DNAH9, and DNAI2 were absent from the respiratory cilia of patients with DNAAF3 mutations.
checks.evidence_quote: ODA components DNAH5 (Fig. 3), DNAH9 and DNAI2 (see Supplementary Fig. 3 and 4), and IDA light chain DNALI1 (Fig. 4) were all absent from the cilia of affected patients.

checks.claim: Using immunofluorescence, Mitchison et al. (2012) found that the inner dynein arm light chain DNALI1 was absent from the respiratory cilia of patients with DNAAF3 mutations.
checks.evidence_quote: ODA components DNAH5 (Fig. 3), DNAH9 and DNAI2 (see Supplementary Fig. 3 and 4), and IDA light chain DNALI1 (Fig. 4) were all absent from the cilia of affected patients.

checks.claim: In some patients with DNAAF3 mutations, residual DNAH5 and DNALI1 were present in the apical cytoplasm of respiratory cells.
checks.evidence_quote: In some patients, residual DNAH5 and DNALI1 can be seen in the apical cytoplasm, whereas cytoplasmic accumulation of these proteins is not seen in control samples.

checks.claim: The immunofluorescence findings suggested that DNAAF3 is required for the cytoplasmic preassembly of outer and inner dynein arms along the entire axoneme.
checks.evidence_quote: These results suggest that DNAAF3 is important for the assembly of outer and inner dynein arms along the entire length of the axoneme, comprising ODA types 1 and 2 and the DNALI1 containing IDA types.
checks.explanation: The paper draws an assembly conclusion from these findings; it does not specifically say the immunofluorescence results show cytoplasmic preassembly. That inference rests on other data.

paragraphs.text: Mitchison et al. (2012) found that the Chlamydomonas pf22 mutant, which carries a nonsense mutation (Trp79Ter) in the DNAAF3 ortholog, had paralyzed half-length flagella that lacked outer dynein arms and inner dynein arms b and c. The PF22 protein was located only in the cytoplasm. In pf22 cytoplasm, IC2 was hyperabundant and heavy chain-intermediate chain complexes formed abnormally, suggesting that PF22 acts at a later step of dynein preassembly than PF13 and ODA7.

checks.evidence_quote: TGG -> TGA, altering a tryptophan to a nonsense codon (p.Trp79X) and predicting a null allele

checks.claim: The Chlamydomonas pf22 mutant has paralyzed half-length flagella.
checks.evidence_quote: The Chlamydomonas pf22 strain was previously shown to be non-motile, with paralyzed half-length flagella and disrupted ODA assembly.

checks.claim: The flagella of the Chlamydomonas pf22 mutant lack outer dynein arms and inner dynein arms b and c.

checks.explanation: ODA assembly also greatly reduced/missing (Fig. 1 legend).

checks.evidence_quote: whereas ODA intermediate chain IC2 (human DNAI2) is hyper-abundant

checks.evidence_quote: This reduction in HCγ suggests that PF22-dependent chaperone activity may be important for correct association of HCs and ICs.

paragraphs.text: Mitchison et al. (2012) found that morpholino knockdown of dnaaf3 in zebrafish caused immotile olfactory placode cilia with reduced or missing dynein arms. Other defects were body axis curvature, hydrocephalus, pronephric cysts, otolith defects, and left-right patterning defects. About half of dnaaf3MOex8 embryos showed reversed or absent heart looping.

paragraphs.text: In affected members of a UK-Pakistani family (UCL71) with primary ciliary dyskinesia-2, in which the parents were first cousins and which showed linkage to the chromosome 19 locus, Mitchison et al. (2012) identified a homozygous 1-bp insertion in exon 6 of the DNAAF3 gene (c.762_763insT). The insertion was predicted to cause a frameshift and premature termination (Val255CysfsTer12). It was absent from 172 UK-Pakistani control chromosomes and segregated with the disorder.
